description:
Repository initialization completes on Windows, so the calls that begin with it do not fail before reaching what they test.

## Background

On the hosted Windows runner, `jit init --json` terminates with exit status `0xc00000fd` and the message "thread 'main' has overflowed its stack" on standard error. That status is Windows' stack-overflow code. Stdout is empty, so the caller receives no report at all, and every acceptance test in the offline profile-adoption job that begins by initializing a repository fails on that one call.

The same call succeeds on Linux. Windows gives a main thread a smaller default stack than Linux does, so a path that recurses without a bound, or holds a frame proportional to something it reads, can survive one platform and not the other. Which path is unestablished: the process dies before it writes any diagnostic of its own, and no test currently exercises initialization on Windows outside this job.

The offline profile-adoption job is the only Windows coverage the workflow has, so the overflow is invisible to every other job and to the local quality gates.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Repository initialization completes on Windows and reports its result on standard output.
- [hard] REQ-02: The overflowing path is identified, and its depth is bounded by construction rather than by how much stack the platform happens to give the thread.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test fails if that path becomes unbounded again, and the test states which path it covers.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every profile-adoption acceptance test whose failure was this overflow passes on Windows.


## Resolution

Windows support is out of scope for the container that surfaced this: the workflow's Windows leg is removed rather than repaired, so no job observes the defect. The diagnosis above is retained for whoever restores that platform.
title: Complete repository initialization on Windows without overflowing the stack
